summary: JavaScript library that adds an AI agent inside your web page, so users can operate your app by typing commands like 'fill in this form'.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Page Agent is an in-page GUI agent. You add one script or npm package to your web app, and an AI agent can click, type and fill forms on that page from natural-language instructions. It reads the page as text (DOM), so it doesn't need screenshots, multimodal models, a browser extension, Python or a headless browser.
sixtySeconds.problem: Adding an AI copilot to a web product usually means backend work and custom tools. Page Agent runs in the browser on your existing UI.
whoFor: SaaS teams adding an AI copilot
Developers of ERP, CRM and admin systems
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for drop-in integration, text-based page control that works with most models including local ones, and an optional Chrome extension and MCP server for multi-page tasks.
requirements: A web app you can add JavaScript to
An LLM endpoint and API key (OpenAI-compatible)

overview: For a quick test, add the demo script tag from jsDelivr, which uses a free testing LLM meant for evaluation only. Add ?autoInit=false to load it without starting the demo agent.
For real use, install the npm package, create a PageAgent with your model, base URL and API key, then call execute with an instruction such as 'Click the login button'.
It is built for client-side web enhancement, not server-side automation, and its DOM processing is derived from browser-use. It is MIT licensed.
limitations: Demo LLM is for evaluation only
Client-side only, not for server automation
